text:
Jordan Kyrou's first season in Washington has hit a pause. The Capitals say he's out at least a week with an upper-body injury, per Daily Faceoff and NHL.com's Tom Gulitti. He goes to the sidelines in a quiet spell: no points in seven straight games, while Washington lost five in a row.

The drought isn't really on him. The chances were there (about 4.1 expected points' worth over those seven games), and the Capitals have scored 10.1 fewer goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice, which has cost him assists and usually swings back. For the season he has 5 goals and 14 points in 21 games on 14:21 a night, seven of the points on the power play.

The rest of his profile is better than his role. Evolving-Hockey had him in the 99th percentile of forwards at taking chances away last season and the 96th at creating them, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 56% of his entries. That's a lot of player for 14 minutes a night, and the question when he returns is whether Washington gives him more.
